warnings: Upper limit 400 µg/day from food plus supplements (NIH ODS); ICMR-NIN TUL Not found; EFSA 2023 reported as 255 µg (secondary, unverified).
Brazil nuts vary hugely in selenium (about 10-100 µg per nut in different reports, single nuts up to thousands); limit to 1-2 nuts and not daily.
IFCT selenium 0 means not analysed, not zero (mushrooms, ghee, oils, refined flour, fresh coconut, ripe tomato, brinjal); do not count as zero.
Do not use IFCT amaranth leaves (C002-C006, about 10 times other greens) or the prawn rows S008/S010; use Q007 for prawns.
IFCT wheat atta (53.1 µg/100 g) is above the highest value in a north-west India wheat survey (27.2 µg/100 g); treat as regional, not a national average.
Raw milled rice in IFCT is 1.0 µg/100 g (low-confidence); rice-based diets may supply little selenium.
Selenium supplements for Hashimoto's are not recommended by current ETA guidance; evidence limited; no quick-add for thyroid-condition users unless doctor-prescribed.
Signs of too much: garlic breath, metallic taste, brittle hair or nails, hair loss, nausea; see a doctor.
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, blood thinners, statin-niacin, chemotherapy and thyroid disease: follow your doctor's advice before any selenium supplement.
